author: Told by Sigrun the Ferrywoman
pages:
#A Tale Told at the River Crossing

My grandmother ran this ferry before me, and her mother before her. She told this story to every passenger who asked why our family never prays at roadside shrines. I tell it now to you.

#The Fisherman

There was a fisherman named Olaf who wanted his nets to always be full. One evening he found a shrine on a sandbar where there had never been a sandbar before. A voice asked him what he desired, and he told it.

The voice agreed. From that day on Olaf's nets came up heavy every single time. He grew rich. He bought a second boat, then a third.

#The Cost

But his nets were always full, and never with anything else. He could not stop catching fish. When he cast a net to rescue a child who had fallen from the pier, it came up full of herring and the child was lost.

When he tried to give up fishing, the fish began to appear in his bed, his boots, his soup. They filled his house until his family left him.

#The End of Olaf

Olaf went back to the sandbar and begged the voice to take the gift away. The voice was very polite. It said that a bargain is a bargain, and that he had asked for full nets, not for happiness.

He was found in the spring, sitting on the sandbar, surrounded by fish that had not spoiled. The sandbar was gone the next morning.

#My Grandmother's Advice

When a voice offers you exactly what you want, ask yourself what it wants. Then ask again. Then row away.
